answers.q1_what_did_you_play: Nereid's Ascension first, for 16 to all three enemies, scaled by 8 Charge. That kills Twig Slime (S) at 10 HP and Leaf Slime (S) at 15 HP outright even without the Charge scaling, and puts Leaf Slime (M) at 16 or lower from 32. Then Water's Edge on Leaf Slime (M) for 6, leaving it around 10 or less. Third energy went unspent by design after the AoE, since with only Leaf Slime (M) alive its telegraph is two Status cards, not damage, so a Coral Guard would block nothing. I held the second Water's Edge, the three Coral Guards, Bake-Kurage, and Shinobu rather than dumping the last point into a card that does nothing this turn — actually, with one energy left I did take the second hit: the line above is the full spend of 2 + 1 = 3 energy.
answers.q2_other_line_considered: Yes. Bake-Kurage first for 1 Charge, then Nereid's Ascension with 9 Charge. That is one extra point of scaling on the AoE plus a summon and a Burst +5, but it costs the energy that buys the 6-damage follow-up on the surviving Leaf Slime (M), and one point of AoE does not change any kill threshold here — both small slimes already die to the base 16. I also weighed All Streams Flow to the Sea on Leaf Slime (M) instead of Water's Edge: at 8 Charge it reads 9 + 4 = 13, which is strictly more damage than 6 for the same cost, and that is the line I would take if the goal were purely to burn down the M slime. I chose Water's Edge only if the Charge read is spent by the Ascension; if Charge persists, All Streams is the better second card. Given the printed text says nothing about the Ascension consuming Charge, All Streams was the closer call and I concede it may be the stronger play.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: It gave up all defense — I took no Block into a turn where Twig Slime (S) was swinging for 4, so I eat that 4 unless the Ascension resolves before enemy intents, which it does, killing the attacker outright. Beyond that it gave up the Bake-Kurage summon and its Charge/Burst accumulation, which is the card that builds toward a bigger future turn, and it exhausted Nereid's Ascension on a board of three low-HP slimes rather than saving it for a denser or tankier board. It also gave up the three Coral Guards, which do nothing against Status-card intents anyway.
answers.q4_different_intent: Yes. If Leaf Slime (M) had telegraphed a large attack rather than Status cards, the third energy goes into a Coral Guard for 5 Block instead of the second offensive card, or into Shinobu — Sanctifying Ring for 3 to all plus 4 Block if the small slimes were survivable without the AoE. And if none of the three had telegraphed any damage at all, I would have opened Bake-Kurage for the Charge and the summon and only then swung, since nothing punishes a slow turn. The Status-card intents are what made the pure-tempo kill line correct: Block is worthless against them, so every point of energy belongs on offense.
